info.name: RAUW Backend API
info.description: Backend-only RAUW API collection. Starts with bearer token authentication requests and can be expanded as new backend endpoints are added.

item.name: Auth

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and officer profile', function () {

request.description: Register a backend API-only officer account with username, email, password, confirm_password, badge_number, department_ids, and optional district_ids. department_ids is required, must contain at least one active department ID (is_active=true), and cannot contain duplicates; inactive or unknown department IDs return 422. district_ids may be omitted or empty, must contain active existing district IDs when present, and cannot contain duplicates; assignments are stored through district_officer. The 201 response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned safe officer profile with departments and districts as compact arrays. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables. Change username, email, and badge_number before rerunning because username and badge_number must be unique within officers and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and user profile', function () {

request.description: Register a public API user account with username, email, password, and confirm_password. The 201 response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned safe user profile that does not duplicate actor_type or expose internal auth fields. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables. Change username and email before rerunning because username must be unique within users and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

exec: const genericMessage = 'The provided credentials could not be registered.';
pm.test('Email error is generic (no email enumeration)', function () {

request.description: Smoke test for anti-enumeration registration errors. Uses a seeded local email (demo.user@example.com) with a new username. Expects 422 with errors.email containing the generic message "The provided credentials could not be registered." — not Laravel's default "already been taken" wording. Does not store a token.

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and profile', function () {

request.description: Authenticate with email and password only. The response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned profile. actor_type is only present at the top level; profile omits internal auth fields. Officer and manager profiles expose assigned departments and districts as compact arrays. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables.

exec: pm.test('Authenticated actor is main manager', function () {

request.description: Log in as the seeded main manager (demo.manager@example.com / password locally). Stores access_token and main_manager_access_token for main-manager-only folders (Managers, department mutations). Ordinary manager flows use manager_access_token after a separate login.

Return the authenticated actor_type and cleaned safe profile payload. actor_type is only present at the top level; profile omits internal auth fields. Officer and manager profiles expose assigned departments and districts as compact arrays. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Self-service identity PATCH for users, officers, and managers. Send only fields to change. Active: username, email, password; officers may also send badge_number. Inactive: username and password only (email and badge_number return 422). Privileged and assignment fields are rejected with 422. When password is present, confirm_password must match.

exec: pm.test('Inactive actor blocked on protected route', function () {

request.description: Smoke test for global inactive-actor middleware. Set inactive_access_token to a bearer token for an actor you deactivated (is_active=false) after login. Expects 403 with message "This account is inactive." Whitelisted routes while inactive: GET/PATCH /api/auth/me (identity), POST /api/auth/logout — compare with Current Profile (200) using the same token.

Invalidate all Sanctum personal access tokens for the authenticated actor (every session ends, not only the bearer token on this request). Requires Authorization: Bearer <token>. Inactive actors may still call logout (whitelisted). After 200, previously issued tokens—including tokens stored in other clients—no longer authenticate.

item.description: Authentication requests for user, officer, and manager actors. Inactive accounts: a valid bearer token for a deactivated actor receives 403 (message: "This account is inactive.") on most protected routes, but may still call Get Me, Logout, and PATCH /api/auth/me for profile recovery. PATCH /api/auth/me/districts and operational APIs (e.g. List Issues) return 403 while inactive. To test: deactivate an actor in the database, log in before deactivation or reuse an existing token, then call Get Me (200) vs a protected route such as List Issues (403).

item.name: Managers

request.description: List managers with is_main_manager=true as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> from Auth / Login with the demo main manager locally (demo.manager@example.com). Results are ordered by username ascending and include departments and districts compact arrays. Pagination uses page and per_page (default 20, max 100). Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Update another main manager's username, email, and/or password as an authenticated active main manager. Send only fields to change. When password is present, confirm_password must match. Privileged fields (is_main_manager, is_active, created_by_manager_id, department_ids, district_ids) are rejected with 422. Path target must have is_main_manager=true; ordinary managers and unknown ids return 404. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Deactivate a main manager (is_active=false) as an authenticated active main manager. Path target must have is_main_manager=true; ordinary managers and unknown ids return 404. Returns 409 when disabling the last active main manager. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Reactivate a main manager (is_active=true) as an authenticated active main manager. Path target must have is_main_manager=true; ordinary managers and unknown ids return 404. Re-enabling an already active main manager is idempotent and returns 200. Unlike disable, no last-active-main-manager guard applies. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

List managers with is_main_manager=false as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> from Auth / Login with the demo main manager locally (demo.manager@example.com). Results are ordered by username ascending and include departments and districts compact arrays. Pagination uses page and per_page (default 20, max 100). Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

exec: pm.test('Response contains created manager profile only', function () {

request.description: Create an ordinary manager as the authenticated main manager. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> from an active manager with is_main_manager=true. department_ids is required, must contain at least one active department ID (is_active=true), and cannot contain duplicates; inactive or unknown department IDs return 422. Manager department assignments are stored through the department_manager pivot. Optional district_ids must contain active existing districts and are stored through district_manager. The 201 response returns the created manager profile only, including departments and districts as compact arrays, and does not include or store an access_token. The new manager must log in separately through Auth / Login. Change username and email before rerunning because username must be unique within managers and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

Update another ordinary manager's username, email, and/or password as an authenticated active main manager. Send only fields to change. When password is present, confirm_password must match. Privileged fields (is_main_manager, is_active, created_by_manager_id, department_ids, district_ids) are rejected with 422. Path target must have is_main_manager=false; main manager IDs and unknown ids return 404. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Deactivate an ordinary manager (is_active=false) as an authenticated active main manager. Path target must have is_main_manager=false; main manager IDs and unknown ids return 404. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Reactivate an ordinary manager (is_active=true) as an authenticated active main manager. Path target must have is_main_manager=false; main manager IDs and unknown ids return 404. Re-enabling an already active manager is idempotent and returns 200. Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403.

Implemented self-service district assignment endpoint for active managers and active officers. Replace the authenticated actor's own district assignments. Users do not have district assignments and receive 403. district_ids must be present, may be an empty array to clear assignments, must contain active existing district IDs, and cannot contain duplicates. Returns the refreshed auth profile with a districts array. This only updates actor district pivots and never modifies issues.district_id.

Manager-admin district assignment endpoint. Replace an officer's district assignments as an authenticated active manager. Users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests cannot update officer districts. district_ids must be present, may be empty to clear assignments, must contain active existing district IDs in the officer's hub when hub_id is set, and cannot contain duplicates; cross-hub IDs return 422. Returns the officer's refreshed profile with districts. This only updates district_officer and never modifies issues.district_id.
Assign a hub to an officer and clear district_officer pivot. Active manager only. Returns refreshed officer auth profile.

Main-manager-only department assignment endpoint. Replace an officer's department assignments as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, inactive main managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403. Unlike Update Officer Districts, non-main managers cannot call this endpoint. department_ids must be present, may be an empty array to clear assignments, must reference active department IDs (is_active=true), and cannot contain duplicates; inactive or unknown IDs return 422. Returns the officer's refreshed auth profile (actor_type + profile) with departments. Soft-deleted officers return 404. This only updates department_officer.

Main-manager-only department assignment endpoint. Replace a manager's department assignments as an authenticated active main manager. department_ids must be present, may be [] to clear all assignments, must reference active department IDs (is_active=true), and cannot contain duplicates; inactive or unknown IDs return 422. Returns the refreshed Manager resource (flat manager profile with departments and districts). Soft-deleted managers return 404. Use the main manager token from Auth / Login (demo.manager@example.com locally). Ordinary managers receive 403.

Main-manager-only district assignment endpoint. Replace a manager's district assignments as an authenticated active main manager. district_ids must be present, may be [] to clear all assignments, must reference active district IDs (is_active=true) in the manager's hub when hub_id is set, and cannot contain duplicates; cross-hub or unknown IDs return 422. Returns the refreshed Manager resource (flat manager profile with departments and districts). The path target must have is_main_manager=false; main managers and unknown ids return 404. Soft-deleted managers return 404. This only updates district_manager and never modifies issues.district_id or officer district pivots. Use the main manager token from Auth / Login (demo.manager@example.com locally). Ordinary managers receive 403.
Assign a hub to a main manager and clear district_manager pivot. Main manager only. Path target must have is_main_manager=true.
Assign a hub to an ordinary manager and clear district_manager pivot. Main manager only. Path target must have is_main_manager=false.

item.description: Protected manager administration requests. Run Auth / Login as Main Manager first so main_manager_access_token is set. List/create/update/disable/enable main managers and ordinary managers use main_manager_access_token. Update Officer Districts accepts any active manager token (access_token after Login). Update Officer Departments, Update Manager Departments, and Sync manager districts require main_manager_access_token. manager_id defaults to 2 locally and is overwritten by Create Manager.

item.name: Officers

query.description: Use true/1 for active-only or false/0 for inactive-only; omit for default active-only.

request.description: List officers as an authenticated active officer or manager. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> from Auth / Login with demo.officer@example.com or a manager account locally. Results are ordered by username ascending and include departments and districts as compact arrays. Soft-deleted officers are excluded. When is_active is omitted, only active officers are returned; use is_active=0 or is_active=false for inactive officers only. Optional district_id and department_id filters narrow results through officer pivots. Pagination uses page and per_page (default 20, max 100). Users and inactive actors receive 403.

Deactivate an officer (is_active=false) as an authenticated active manager. Users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403. Returns the refreshed Officer resource with departments and districts. Does not soft-delete the row. Soft-deleted officers return 404. Use any active manager token from Auth / Login.

Reactivate an officer (is_active=true) as an authenticated active manager. Users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403. Re-enabling an already active officer is idempotent and returns 200. Does not restore soft-deleted officers (404). Returns the refreshed Officer resource with departments and districts. Use any active manager token from Auth / Login.

Implemented officer self-service district assignment flow. Replace the authenticated officer's district assignments through district_officer. district_ids must be an array of active existing district IDs without duplicates; use an empty array to clear assignments. Returns the refreshed auth profile with districts and never modifies issues.district_id.

item.description: Officer-focused request examples. List officers is available to active officers and managers. Disable and enable officer require an active manager token (access_token after Login as a manager). The district self-service update entry is implemented for active officers.

item.name: Categories

request.description: List categories as any authenticated actor. Main categories are ordered by priority (lower = higher urgency); subcategories are ordered alphabetically by name. Responses include assigned departments from the category_department pivot.
Show one category with parent, children when loaded, and assigned departments. Any authenticated actor may call this endpoint.

Create a main category as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Ordinary managers receive 403. Main categories use priority; lower values sort first. department_ids must contain existing departments.

Create a subcategory under an active main category as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. Nested subcategories are rejected. Subcategories order alphabetically by name; weight is rejected with 422.

Partially update a category as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. If department_ids is present, it replaces the category's pivot assignments. parent_id may only reference a main category; subcategories cannot have children.

Standard safe removal path via generic PATCH as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. Sets is_active=false while keeping the category row, department assignments, and historical issue references intact.
Reactivate an inactive category via generic PATCH with is_active=true as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403.

Guarded hard delete for eligible categories only as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. Prefer Deactivate Category (PATCH is_active=false). A main category with subcategories returns 409 with message about subcategories; categories referenced by existing issues also return 409.

item.name: Hard Delete Main Category With Subcategories (409)

request.description: Negative example. DELETE a main category that still has subcategories returns 409: Cannot delete a main category while it still has subcategories.

item.description: Category management requests. Reads work for any authenticated actor; POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE require an authenticated active main manager (main_manager_access_token). Categories use a two-level hierarchy (main + subcategory only). Main categories use priority; subcategories order alphabetically by name. Activation and deactivation use generic PATCH with is_active; hard delete is guarded.

item.name: Hubs

request.description: List Rotterdam cluster hubs ordered by name with district, officer, and manager reference counts. Any authenticated actor may call this endpoint.
Show one hub with reference counts. Any authenticated actor may call this endpoint. Locally hub_id 3 is Cluster Centrum.
Create a hub as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403.
Partially update a hub as an authenticated active main manager.
Hard delete an eligible hub as an authenticated active main manager. Returns 409 when districts, officers, or managers still reference the hub.

item.description: Hub CRUD requests. Reads work for any authenticated actor; POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE require main_manager_access_token. Seeded hubs: Cluster Zuid, Cluster Buitengebieden, Cluster Centrum (id 3), Cluster Noord.

item.name: Districts

request.description: List districts ordered by name with hub metadata, manager/officer assignment counts, and issue reference counts. Requires authentication in the protected API group. Managers and officers use many-to-many district pivots; issues.district_id remains a singular issue location/reference field.
Show one district with manager/officer assignment counts and issue reference count. Requires authentication.

Create a district as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). hub_id is required and must reference an existing hub (use hub_id env var, Cluster Centrum=3 locally). Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403. Use main_manager_access_token; manager_access_token from a non-main manager should fail with 403.
Update a district as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. Supports partial updates for name, hub_id, postal_prefix, center_lat, center_lng, and radius_meters.
Deactivate a district via generic PATCH with is_active=false. Requires main_manager_access_token. No dedicated /disable route exists.
Reactivate an inactive district via generic PATCH with is_active=true. Requires main_manager_access_token.

Delete an eligible district as an authenticated active main manager. Ordinary managers receive 403. Returns 409 Conflict while the district is assigned to managers, assigned to officers, or referenced by issues through issues.district_id.

item.description: District CRUD requests. Reads require authentication; POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE require an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Ordinary managers receive 403 on district writes. Activation and deactivation use generic PATCH with is_active only (no /disable route). Actor district assignments are many-to-many through district_manager and district_officer. Issue district handling is out of scope: issues.district_id remains singular.

item.name: Issues

exec: pm.test('Issue has derived departments, required district, and safe author', function () {

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Parkeren op stoep",
  "content": "Er staat een auto op de stoep bij Coolsingel.",
  "category_id": {{category_id}},
  "district_id": {{district_id}},
  "postal_code": "3012AB",
  "address": "Coolsingel 1, Rotterdam",
  "latitude": 51.91712,
  "longitude": 4.47834,
  "is_anonymous": true
}

request.description: Create an issue as an authenticated active user. Required fields are title, content, category_id, and district_id. Do not send department: issue departments are derived server-side from the selected category, stored through the department_issue pivot, and returned as a read-only departments array. Optional location fields are postal_code, address, latitude, and longitude. Removed legacy locality fields are not accepted. Anonymous issues remain owned through issues.user_id; the backend generates a stable alias such as Melder#A1B2C3D4 and does not accept anonymous_alias from clients. The test stores issue_id for follow-up requests.

query.description: Composable filter by real department code; matches issues where any assigned department has this code

request.description: List issues for an authenticated actor. district_id, department, and category_id are optional and composable; combine any subset to narrow results. Query param department (Postman env department_filter) must be an existing department code; filtering uses department_issue with any-match semantics. Do not send department on create/update bodies. Pagination is backend-driven with page and per_page; per_page defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

query.description: Active users only: restrict to issues owned by the authenticated user (issues.user_id), including own hidden issues

request.description: List only issues owned by the authenticated active user. Requires a user bearer token; officers and managers receive 422 when mine is set. Composes with default user visibility scoping and optional district_id, department, and category_id filters.

query.description: Officers and managers only: narrow list to hidden issues. Users receive 422.

request.description: Officer/manager visibility filter smoke test. Log in as demo.officer@example.com or a manager before running. Query param visibility=hidden returns only hidden issues; omit visibility to see all issues. Active users cannot use visibility and receive 422. Composes with district_id, department, and category_id filters.

query.description: Composable status filter for any active actor. Valid values: open, in_behandeling, opgelost, gesloten. Invalid values return 422.

request.description: Filter issues by status. Available to users, officers, and managers. Composes with default visibility scoping and optional district_id, department, category_id, mine, and visibility filters.

query.description: Officers and managers only: restrict to issues assigned to this officer id. Users receive 422. Mutually exclusive with unassigned.

request.description: Officer/manager assignee filter smoke test. Log in as demo.officer@example.com or a manager before running. Replace assigned_officer_id=1 with a real officer id from your database. Composes with status, visibility, district_id, department, and category_id filters.

query.description: Officers and managers only: restrict to issues with no assigned officer (assigned_officer_id is null). Users receive 422. Mutually exclusive with assigned_officer_id.

request.description: Officer/manager unassigned filter smoke test. Log in as demo.officer@example.com or a manager before running. Query param unassigned=1 returns only issues without an assigned officer. Composes with status, visibility, district_id, department, and category_id filters.

Show one issue with derived read-only departments plus category, district, and attachment summaries when loaded. The response exposes departments as an array only and does not include a singular department field. Authenticated request only. Anonymous issues expose an author display alias and not the owning user id.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Stoeptegel bij bushalte bijgewerkt",
  "content": "De tegel ligt nu volledig los.",
  "category_id": {{category_id}},
  "district_id": {{district_id}},
  "is_anonymous": false
}

request.description: Partially update an issue owned by the authenticated active user. Ownership is checked through issues.user_id, including anonymous issues. Editable fields are title, content, category_id, district_id, postal_code, address, latitude, longitude, and is_anonymous. Do not send department: when category_id changes, departments are re-derived from that category and returned as a read-only departments array. Attachments are changed separately: delete existing attachments first when replacement is needed, then use Upload Attachments.

Set issue visibility to visible or hidden. Active officers and managers only; users receive 403. The issue must be viewable by the caller (same rules as Show Issue); otherwise the API returns 404. Log in as demo.officer@example.com or a manager before running. User-owned PATCH /api/issues/{issue_id} cannot change visibility.

exec: pm.test('Response wraps attachments in data array', function () {

formdata.description: Choose 1-5 files. Each file must be <= 5 MB and one of jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, or pdf.

request.description: Upload attachments to an issue owned by the authenticated active user. Each issue may hold at most 5 attachments total. Each file is limited to 5 MB. Files are stored on local non-public development storage and are downloaded only through authenticated endpoints. The 201 response wraps attachments as data: [...]. The test stores attachment_id and attachment_download_url from response.data[0].

Owner-only attachment deletion. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> for the active regular user who owns the issue. The attachment must belong to the issue in the route. A successful request returns 204 No Content, removes the backing file from non-public local storage when present, and hard deletes the attachment row. Use before Upload Attachments when replacing files.
Authenticated attachment download. The attachment must belong to the issue in the route and the local backing file must exist. The API streams the original filename from non-public local storage.

Hard delete an issue owned by the authenticated active user. This is not a soft delete: the issue row is removed and attachments cascade with the issue. Run after attachment examples if you want to preserve issue_id for follow-up requests.

item.description: Authenticated issue CRUD and attachment examples. Issue creation requires district_id and no longer accepts client-supplied department or removed legacy locality fields. Departments are derived from the selected category, stored in department_issue, and exposed as a read-only departments array. List filters are composable: district_id, department (code), category_id, mine (users only), and visibility (officers/managers only). Department filtering uses any-match semantics; pagination is backend-driven. Show returns 404 when the issue is not visible to the actor (e.g. another user's hidden issue). Anonymous issues retain user_id ownership while exposing only a stable alias. Attachment deletion is owner-only for replacement workflows. Issue deletion is hard delete and attachments cascade with the issue.

item.name: Departments

request.description: List departments from the departments table with category counts. Requires authentication in the protected API group.
Show one department with category count. Requires authentication in the protected API group.

Create a department. Requires an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Ordinary managers, users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests cannot mutate departments.
Update department code or name. Requires an authenticated active main manager.
Safe department removal path via generic PATCH with is_active=false. Requires main_manager_access_token. Prefer this over hard delete when historical category/issue context must remain.
Reactivate an inactive department via generic PATCH with is_active=true. Requires main_manager_access_token.
Negative example. PATCH is_active=false returns 409 when the department is still referenced by existing records: Cannot disable this department because it is still referenced by existing records.

Delete a department as an authenticated active main manager. Departments assigned to any manager or officer return 409 until those actor assignments are changed. After no actors reference the department, database cascade removes category_department and department_issue assignments automatically; category and issue records remain intact.

item.description: Department CRUD requests. Department mutations require an authenticated active main manager (main_manager_access_token). Activation and deactivation use generic PATCH with is_active only; hard delete is guarded when managers/officers still reference the row. Managers use department_ids through the department_manager pivot and must have one or more departments; officers use department_ids through the department_officer pivot and must have one or more departments. Deleting a department is blocked while assigned to managers or officers; otherwise it removes category_department and department_issue pivot assignments automatically but does not delete categories or issues. Issue departments are derived from categories and exposed to clients as read-only departments arrays.
